Notes: First Jewish immigrants arrived between 1840 and 1860 according to records of the Cementerio de Disidentes de Valparaíso; year = midpoint of range
First documented individual: Manuel de Lima y Sola (Jew of European origin) was a founding member of the Valparaíso Fire Department in 1851; first Jews in Valparaíso were from Germany and France
Manuel de Lima founded in Valparaíso the first Spanish-speaking Masonic lodge in 1853; source says Jews of various origins settled in the port from the early 19th century
Census: only 20 persons of Jewish religion lived in the area of the present V Region of Valparaíso up to 1907 (regional aggregate, not the city alone)
Turkish (Smyrna) Sephardic Jews arrived in Valparaíso around 1910; about 1916 the Turkish and Russian groups separated
Max Nordau society founded in 1916, the first Jewish organization in Valparaíso, uniting Sephardim and Ashkenazim
'Hundreds of Turkish and Russian Jewish families' formed the Sociedad Israelita Max Nordau in 1916 (vague journalistic figure, not used as Population); synagogue moved to Viña del Mar in the 1930s
Sociedad Max Nordau founded in Valparaíso in 1916

General assembly of Sociedad Max Nordau on 29 May 1919 attended by 25 members (socios); society described as 'very small'; 14 Russian Jewish women in transit to Buenos Aires assisted (subset/transit counts - not population)
Census 1920: 261 persons of Jewish religion in the V Region of Valparaíso (regional aggregate)
Split of Ashkenazim from Max Nordau: Sociedad Unión Israelita founded 3 December 1922 at a meeting of 25 persons (founding members - subset); Jewish cemetery mausoleum operational 1924

A 1929 correspondent wrote that 'in less than three years the 120 families that composed our collectivity' were reduced to a quarter (~600 persons if x5); unclear whether this covers the whole Valparaíso community or only the Ashkenazi Unión Israelita circle (which held ~60% of the community) - left blank; year = ~3 years before 1929
Per the same 1929 correspondent the 120 families had been reduced to one quarter (~30 families; ~150 if x5) through emigration; scope uncertain (community vs Ashkenazi circle) - left blank
Comunidad Habonim of German Jews created in 1939 (refugees from Nazism); Sociedad Unión Israelita de Beneficencia founded 1922
Colegio Hebreo founded in 1947; Wizo 1937; 1938-1939 new immigration wave; synagogue and community seats were on calle Deformes and calle Victoria in Valparaíso
Census 1952: 843 persons of Jewish religion in the V Region of Valparaíso (regional aggregate; second largest after Santiago region)

Community census 1954: 'had in the city a little over 1,000 Jews grouped in 330 families' (Senderey 1956); the accompanying table is titled Comunidad Judía Valparaíso-Viña del Mar so may include Viña del Mar
Comunidad Israelita de Valparaíso-Viña del Mar formed in 1961 by merger; since 1961 the synagogue is in Viña del Mar

Community census 1981: organized Valparaíso-Viña del Mar community of 540 persons plus about 80 unaffiliated Jews with their families; regional total 'little over 600' (metro/regional and membership figures - not city population)
Max Nordau (Sephardic) community in Valparaíso celebrated its centenary in 2016; community located at General Cruz 960
Max Nordau described as the only synagogue in Valparaíso and 103 years old (year computed 1916+103)
'At present the community consists of approximately 120 families' (Valparaíso-Viña del Mar community; ~600 if x5; metro-area membership - not city population); year = article publication 2021
